repair_notes.consumer_counterexample: Let d=1, lambda(dx)=w(x)dx for a strictly positive smooth nonconstant probability density w (e.g. standard Gaussian), pi=delta_0, rho_t(x|0)=1, u_t(x|0)=1/w(x). All fields and their compact-local derivatives are smooth and bounded on each compact, and the revised measure identity holds because rho lambda is stationary and rho u lambda=dx has zero distributional divergence. Yet partial_t rho+partial_x(rho u)=(1/w)′ is not identically zero. The single-endpoint marginal has p=1 and J=1/w, giving the same failure. For the gradient theorem choose a parameter-independent v=u, so both losses and C and all parameter derivative majorants vanish; the unweighted marginal PDE still fails. This is a counterexample to reading the revised general measure premise as implying the classical conclusion, not to the algebraic loss identity.
